short: Lip-timed phonemes into a codec LM (M06) are standard; Chem WER edges EmoDubber 12.5% vs 12.8%, and sync is shown only by MCD-DTW-SL, with gains Table 1 does not support.
position: VSpeechLM [@wang2025vspeechlm] changes one component, synthesis (M06): a per-frame phoneme aligner feeds a pretrained codec language model instead of a duration-based, diffusion or flow decoder. Both halves are standard: lip-set phoneme durations without a duration predictor appear in Hegde et al. [@hegde2023towards] (§3.2.2), and the authors themselves cite an earlier speech-LLM dubbing system (§2.1). The content gain over the strongest baseline is small, 12.5% against 12.8% WER on Chem (Table 1), while the [concurrent] DiFlowDubber reports 9.65% against 11.72% for the same baseline [@nguyen2026diflowdubber]. The synchronization claim is the weakest: it rests on a length-weighted spectral distance alone (§4.1), its headline reductions do not follow from Table 1, and on GRID the method ties EmoDubber on that metric. On lip sync the evaluation (M12) is weaker than every other text-and-video study in the Appendix population.
